title: Probe fence_spans mishandled unclosed code fences (explicit null end_line)
observed: scripts/disc002_batch14_probe.py crashed with TypeError: '<=' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'NoneType' while probing the mermaid-color term family ('fill:#'): a file with an UNCLOSed code fence produced a fence span whose end element was None.
expected_condition: Every code-fence span used by the fence-aware probe must be a (start, end) pair of integers; an unclosed fence extends to EOF.
root_cause: mdextract reports end_line=null with closed=false for unclosed fences; the probe's fence_spans used f.get('end_line', start), which only defaults when the KEY is absent — an explicit JSON null slips through as None. The batch-10..13 probes (and their docstring comment 'mdextract reports end_line as the last line') share the latent defect.
evidence: src/vault_unification/mdextract.py _flush_fence (end_line None when unclosed, 'closed': end_line is not None, lines 153-167); the session-14 crash traceback in the tool log; the fixed scripts/disc002_batch14_probe.py fence_spans(struct, total_lines).
impact: Batches 10-13 were NOT affected in practice: no probed term in those tranches matched a definition pattern inside an unclosed fence, so no heading/def classification changed. Had it triggered, an in-fence '#'-comment or def-pattern hit could have been misclassified as out-of-fence coverage evidence.
repair: fence_spans now takes total_lines and maps end_line None -> total_lines (span extends to EOF). Applied in scripts/disc002_batch14_probe.py; future probe scripts must copy the batch-14 pattern, not the batch-13 one.
verification: The fixed probe re-ran to completion: 290 terms, exit 0, results at scratch/disc002-batch14-probe.json. The 173 pre-fix OK verify checks were unaffected (fence classification identical for all closed-fence files).
regression_prevention: Batch-15+ probe scripts MUST use the F-0021-fixed fence_spans signature (struct, total_lines). Optionally add a unit test with an unclosed-fence fixture if the probe logic is promoted into the framework package.
remaining_risk: The batch-10..13 probe scripts in the repo still contain the latent defect (historical artifacts, not re-run); their JSON results remain valid per the impact analysis.

title: Registry destinations UNIQUE(path, heading) cannot dedupe NULL headings (row-per-insert duplication)
discovered_by: DISP-001 session 19 (2026-11-01), via kureg-validate orphan_destination warnings
observed: After the first kureg-apply-dispositions run, the derived registry contained 28,754 destinations rows for 544 distinct canonical paths and 28,210 orphan_destination warnings.
expected_condition: One destinations row per distinct (path, heading); applying N ledger records referencing the same NULL-heading destination creates exactly one row.
root_cause: In SQL, NULL is distinct from NULL inside UNIQUE indexes, so INSERT OR IGNORE INTO destinations (path, heading) with heading = NULL inserts a new row on every call; the kureg-load destination loader and the new apply_dispositions shared the pattern (kureg-load never triggered it because extracted KU records carry no destinations).
evidence: Direct SQL census before the fix: destinations rows 28,754, edges 28,754, orphan rows 28,210, dup-path example ('01 - Foundations/AI ML and DL Hierarchy/AI vs ML vs DL.md', None, 124).
impact: Derived-registry corruption only (the registry DB is rebuildable and git-ignored); the committed ledger and mapping were unaffected. The first apply linked each KU to the first-created row for its path, so effective dispositions and edges were still correct — the damage was duplicate/orphan rows and noisy validation warnings.
repair: New _upsert_destination(conn, path, heading) helper (SELECT-first, insert only when absent) used by both kureg-load's destination loader and kureg-apply-dispositions; the derived registry was rebuilt from committed state.
verification: Rebuilt registry: 544 destinations rows, 28,754 edges, 0 orphans, kureg-validate valid=True with 0 errors and 0 warnings; regression test test_f0023_null_heading_destinations_do_not_duplicate in tests/test_dispositions.py.
regression_prevention: Any future code inserting into destinations must use _upsert_destination, never INSERT OR IGNORE (NULL heading defeats the unique constraint).
remaining_risk: None known.

title: Heading-convention check treated year-initial headings (timelines) as numbered headings
discovered_by: session-22 area-07 audit (51 mixed-numbering-scheme findings across 2 notes)
observed: Notes faithfully preserving their sources' timeline headings ('### 2014 (Sept): Seq2Seq', '### 2018+: Modern Attention', '### 2020 and beyond: ...') were flagged as 'unnumbered heading mixed into a numbered note' for EVERY contract-compliant unnumbered heading they contained, because _NUMBERED_HEADING_RE (^(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)[.)]?\s+\S, separator OPTIONAL) matches a leading 4-digit year followed by a space.
root_cause: The regex's optional separator makes any 'YYYY <text>' heading look like section numbering; year-range headings are legitimate chronological content in the sources' history sections, and generated notes preserve them verbatim per the editorial contract.
evidence: reports/synthesis/s22-area07-audit.json first pass: 51 mixed-numbering-scheme findings, all in Origins of Attention.md (21) and Contextual Embeddings ELMo to BERT.md (30), whose only 'numbered' headings are years; verified all 30 four-digit-initial headings vault-wide (sources + output) are years 2013-2026 or quantities like '2048-Token Context', none are section numbers.
repair: omission.py: new _YEAR_LIKE_HEADING_RE + _is_year_like() (leading 4-digit number in 1000-2999); the heading-convention check classifies a heading as numbered only if it matches _NUMBERED_HEADING_RE AND is not year-like; _heading_number_stripped keeps year-initial headings intact (the year is content, not numbering). Dash-style numbering ('04 - vLLM', '13 — Inference MOC') still counts as numbered: 1,307 source headings rely on that and are unaffected.
regression_prevention: tests/test_omission.py TestYearHeadingsNotNumbering: _is_year_like predicate cases (incl. 5-digit '12345 tokens' not a year), _heading_number_stripped keeps years while stripping real numbering, a year-timeline note (unnumbered + year headings) produces ZERO mixed-numbering findings, and a genuine '## 1. Numbered' + '## Unnumbered' mix is STILL flagged.
verification: python3 -m pytest tests/test_omission.py -q -> 44 passed (40 existing + 4 new); vu omission-pilot re-run after the change: 12/12 detection, 12/12 KU localization, 12/12 note localization, 0 false positives (reports/synthesis/s22-omission-pilot-f0032.json); all three area audits valid=true 0 findings
remaining_risk: A genuine section numbered with a bare 4-digit year-range number (e.g. '## 2014. Section') would be misclassified as content; no such heading exists in the corpus or the canonical structure.
